data.name: Lung transplant
data.description: Clinical setting in which mTOR inhibitors are used as antiproliferative, calcineurin-sparing immunosuppression. They are not used de novo: early sirolimus after lung transplantation caused fatal bronchial anastomotic dehiscence, so they are introduced only once the airway anastomosis has healed, and a benefit against chronic lung allograft dysfunction is not established.
data.description_beginner: The situation after a donor lung is implanted, where the immune system has to be held back for life. mTOR inhibitors are used mainly to reduce the dose of the usual drugs and spare the kidneys. They are not started straight after surgery, because early use stopped the airway join from healing, which was fatal in some patients, and whether they slow the long-term scarring that destroys transplanted lungs is still being tested.

studies.title: Does the duration of exposure to everolimus influence the occurrence of chronic lung allograft dysfunction?
studies.authors: Landoas A; Perrier Q; Falque L et al.

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: In lung transplant recipients, later introduction of everolimus and a greater number of treatment interruptions were both risk factors for chronic lung allograft dysfunction; earlier, uninterrupted treatment was associated with lower CLAD risk (retrospective, single-centre; causality not established).
